checklist.item: Images fill their frames via object-fit: cover, no distortion; wide 'Food Hall' exterior crop is reasonable (building/sign visible, not an awkward sliver)

Desktop rendered wide frame 568x872, tall frame 568x1091. Mobile rendered wide frame 350x537, tall frame 350x524. Full-frame screenshots (scrolled to align image top with viewport top, bypassing the sticky nav) confirm the wide crop shows the complete Spanish-tile roof, the 'Food Hall' sign, awning, balcony diners, and street-level bikes/cyclist — not a tight/awkward sliver — at both desktop and mobile. Tall frame shows the full archway with sunlit patio diners and umbrellas at both sizes.
checklist.note: Container class is named .spread-photo-wide but the actual rendered box is portrait-oriented (roughly matching the tall frame's proportions), because the source photo (2026-outside.jpg, 1042x1600) is itself a portrait crop, not a landscape one. This is a design/naming mismatch worth flagging to design, NOT a visual defect — side-by-side the two columns read as balanced, and the crop itself looks intentional and well-composed at both viewports. See minor_notes.

checklist.item: Two-column spread balanced on desktop, stacks cleanly on mobile
checklist.evidence: Desktop: two columns render near-identical width (568px) and near-identical height (872px vs 1091px, close enough to read as a balanced spread, not lopsided). Mobile: paragraph → wide photo → tall photo stack top-to-bottom with consistent gutters/border-radius, no overlap or squeezed spacing.

console_errors: None tied to the 2026 section or the photo swap. Two unrelated, pre-existing 404s for /_vercel/insights/script.js and /_vercel/speed-insights/script.js (Vercel analytics, expected absent on local static server).
minor_notes: Naming/semantic mismatch (non-blocking): the wide frame's CSS class (.spread-photo-wide) implies a landscape image, but the new source (2026-outside.jpg, 1042x1600) is portrait, so the rendered box ends up nearly as tall/portrait as the 'tall' column next to it rather than a wide letterboxed shape. Visually this still reads fine — balanced two-column spread, good crop, no distortion — but if the original design intent was a true wide/landscape frame under the paragraph, flag to design for a source-image re-check (crop a landscape version of 2026-outside, or rename the class to match its new portrait role).

Tooling note for future QA: taking a full-element (--selector) screenshot of this section captures the sticky top nav mid-composite (renders twice, once floating over the photos) because Playwright's element screenshot stitches multiple scroll positions while the nav stays fixed. Not a real user-facing bug — confirmed by re-screenshotting with plain --viewport captures at aligned scroll positions, where the nav appears normally once at the top and the photos render clean underneath.
